questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B fills it in 18 hours. If both are opened together, how many hours will the tank take to fill?
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours, pipe B in 8 hours, and pipe C (a drain) empties it in 24 hours. If all three are open simultaneously, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/6 + 1/8 − 1/24. LCM(6,8,24) = 24. = 4/24 + 3/24 − 1/24 = 6/24 = 1/4. Time = 4 hours. **Short Trick:** Units method: LCM=24. A=4u/h fill, B=3u/h fill, C=1u/h drain. Net=6u/h fill. Time=24/6=4h.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: A tap fills a tank in 10 hours. Due to a leak at the bottom, it takes 12 hours to fill the tank. How many hours does the leak alone take to empty the full tank?
questions.explanation: Fill rate with no leak = 1/10. With leak = 1/12. Leak rate = 1/10 − 1/12 = 6/60 − 5/60 = 1/60. Leak alone empties the tank in 60 hours. **Short Trick:** Leak time = (10×12)/(12−10) = 120/2 = 60 hrs.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 and 20 hours respectively. Both are opened together. After 4 hours, pipe B is closed. In how many total hours will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation: In 4 hours, A+B together fill: 4×(1/15+1/20) = 4×(4+3)/60 = 4×7/60 = 28/60 = 7/15. Remaining = 1−7/15 = 8/15. Only A is open at rate 1/15/h. Time = (8/15)÷(1/15) = 8 more hours. Total = 4+8 = 12 hours. **Short Trick:** LCM(15,20)=60. A=4u/h, B=3u/h. In 4h: 7×4=28u filled. Left=32u. A alone: 32/4=8h. Total=12h.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipes A and B together fill a tank in 6 hours. Pipe A alone takes 10 hours. How long does pipe B alone take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Rate of B = (1/6) − (1/10) = 5/30 − 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. B alone fills in 15 hours. **Short Trick:** B = (A×joint)/(A−joint) = (10×6)/(10−6) = 60/4 = 15 hrs.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. If both pipes are opened together, how many minutes will it take to fill the tank?
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 4 hours, pipe B fills it in 12 hours, and pipe C (a drain) empties it in 6 hours. If all three are open simultaneously, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/4 + 1/12 − 1/6. LCM = 12. = 3/12 + 1/12 − 2/12 = 2/12 = 1/6. Time = 6 hours. Verify: in 1h, net fill = 1/6 of tank; in 6h = full ✓.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipes P and Q together fill a tank in 12 hours. If P alone takes 20 hours, how many hours does Q alone take?
questions.explanation: Rate of Q = 1/12 − 1/20 = 5/60 − 3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30. Q alone fills in 30 hours. **Short Trick:** Q = (P×joint)/(P−joint) = (20×12)/(20−12) = 240/8 = 30 hrs.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 8 hours and pipe B fills it in 16 hours. If both pipes are opened at 9 AM, at what time will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/8 + 1/16 = 2/16 + 1/16 = 3/16. Time = 16/3 hours = 5 hours 20 minutes. Starting from 9 AM: 9 AM + 5h 20min = 2:20 PM. **Short Trick:** T=(8×16)/(8+16)=128/24=16/3h=5h20min → 9AM+5h20min=2:20PM.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: A cistern has a filling pipe (rate 1/6 of tank per hour) and an emptying pipe (rate 1/4 per hour). If both are opened simultaneously on a FULL cistern, what will happen?
questions.explanation: Net rate = fill − empty = 1/6 − 1/4 = 2/12 − 3/12 = −1/12 per hour. Negative means the cistern is draining. From full, it empties at rate 1/12 per hour → empties completely in 12 hours. The emptying pipe (1/4) is faster than the filling pipe (1/6), so the net effect is always draining.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes fill a tank in 24 and 32 minutes. A drain pipe empties it in 16 minutes. If all three are open (tank empty), when will the tank be full?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/24 + 1/32 − 1/16. LCM = 96. = 4/96 + 3/96 − 6/96 = 1/96 per minute. Time = 96 minutes. **Short Trick:** LCM=96. Inlets add: 4+3=7u/min; drain removes 6u/min. Net=1u/min fill rate. Time=96/1=96 min.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipe A (fills in 12 hours) is opened at 8 AM. Pipe B (fills in 8 hours) is opened at 10 AM. At what time will the tank be completely full?
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: A filling pipe fills a tank in 3 hours. The tank is already 1/3 full. How many more hours does the pipe need to fill the tank completely?
questions.explanation: Remaining portion = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3. Rate = 1/3 per hour. Time = (2/3) ÷ (1/3) = 2 hours. **Short Trick:** 2/3 of the job at 1/3 per hour = 2/3 × 3 = 2 hours.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Two fill pipes each take 6 hours to fill a tank. A hole can empty the tank in 4 hours. If both pipes are open but the hole is present, how long does the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/6 + 1/6 − 1/4 = 2/6 − 1/4 = 4/12 − 3/12 = 1/12. Time = 12 hours. Verify: two fill pipes together fill at 1/3/h; hole drains at 1/4/h; net = 1/3−1/4=4/12−3/12=1/12; time=12h ✓.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank 3 times as fast as pipe B. Together they fill the tank in 18 minutes. How many minutes does pipe B alone take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Let B take t minutes → A takes t/3 minutes. Together: 1/(t/3) + 1/t = 3/t + 1/t = 4/t = 1/18. So t = 72 minutes (B alone). A alone = 72/3 = 24 min. **Verify:** together = AB/(A+B) = 24×72/(24+72) = 1728/96 = 18 min ✓.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: A filling pipe fills a tank in 40 minutes. An emptying pipe drains it in 60 minutes. If the tank is half-full and both pipes are opened, how many minutes will it take for the tank to overflow?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate = 1/40 − 1/60 = 3/120 − 2/120 = 1/120 per minute. Remaining capacity = 1/2 of tank. Time = (1/2) ÷ (1/120) = 60 minutes. **Short Trick:** Net rate=1/120/min; half tank = 60 min to fill remaining half → overflow at 60 min.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipes A and B together fill a tank in 8 hours. Both are opened at 6 AM. After 2 hours, pipe B is closed and pipe A continues alone. After pipe B closes, how many more hours does pipe A take, and what is the total time?
questions.explanation: Pipe A fills in 10h, pipe B fills in 40h; together rate = 1/10+1/40 = 4/40+1/40 = 5/40 = 1/8 ✓ (fills in 8h). In 2 hours (A+B): filled = 2×1/8 = 1/4. Remaining = 3/4. A alone at 1/10/h: time = (3/4)÷(1/10) = 7.5 h. Total = 2+7.5 = 9.5 hours.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: A cistern is two-thirds full. A fill pipe fills it in 18 minutes; a drain pipe empties it in 9 minutes. If both are open, in how many minutes will the cistern be completely empty?
questions.explanation: Net drain rate = 1/9 − 1/18 = 2/18 − 1/18 = 1/18 per minute (net emptying because drain > fill). Tank is 2/3 full. Time to empty = (2/3) ÷ (1/18) = (2/3)×18 = 12 minutes. **Short Trick:** Net drain=1/18/min; volume=2/3; time=12 min.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Three pipes can fill a tank in 6, 8, and 12 hours respectively. If all three are opened together, in how long will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/6+1/8+1/12. LCM(6,8,12) = 24. = 4/24+3/24+2/24 = 9/24 = 3/8. Time = 8/3 hours = 2 hours 40 minutes. **Short Trick:** LCM=24; A=4u/h, B=3u/h, C=2u/h → 9u/h; time=24/9=8/3h=2h40min.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank in 5 hours. There is a leakage that empties the tank in 20 hours. With both the pipe open and the leakage present, how long does it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate = 1/5 − 1/20 = 4/20 − 1/20 = 3/20 per hour. Time = 20/3 hours ≈ 6 hours 40 minutes. **Short Trick:** T_net = (5×20)/(20−5) = 100/15 = 20/3 hours.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Three pipes A, B, and C together fill a tank in 3 hours. A alone fills it in 6 hours; B alone in 8 hours. How long does C alone take to fill the tank?
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: One pipe fills a tank in 8 minutes, a second in 12 minutes. How much of the tank is filled in 3 minutes if both pipes are open?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/8 + 1/12 = 3/24 + 2/24 = 5/24 per minute. In 3 minutes: 3 × 5/24 = 15/24 = 5/8 of the tank. **Short Trick:** 5/24 per min × 3 min = 15/24 = 5/8.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: A fill pipe fills a tank in 30 hours. If one-third of the tank is already filled, how long will the pipe take to fill the remaining portion?
questions.explanation: Remaining = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3. Rate = 1/30 per hour. Time = (2/3) ÷ (1/30) = (2/3) × 30 = 20 hours. **Short Trick:** 2/3 of the job at 1/30 per hour = 20 hours.
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipes A+B fill a tank in 6 hours, B+C in 8 hours, A+C in 12 hours. How long does pipe C alone take to fill the tank?
questions.subject: quant

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 3 hours. Pipe B (a drain) empties it in 12 hours. If both are opened on an empty tank, how many hours will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate = 1/3 − 1/12 = 4/12 − 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 per hour. Time = 4 hours. **Short Trick:** T_net = (A×B)/(B−A) = (3×12)/(12−3) = 36/9 = 4 hrs (use B−A since B is larger, meaning it drains faster than A fills).
questions.subject: quant
